federal decree-law 34/2021 art.9 (data destruction/alteration): elements met — unauthorized access to hr information system, data manipulation (stego embedding, copying, destruction of source files), data resided on a computer network. elements missing — formal written authorization matrix, forensic image with documented chain of custody confirming stego payload and deletion artefacts, confirmation deletion was 'without authorization' as distinct act. prosecution strength: strong.

federal decree-law 34/2021 art.2 (unlawful access): elements met — access to information system, access without permission of system owner. elements missing — specific rbac/dlp policy documentation, identity of data controller with formal authorization to restrict access, evidence distinguishing valid-credentials-exceeding-scope from fully unauthorized intrusion. prosecution strength: moderate.

uae penal code art.379 (breach of confidentiality / trade secrets): elements met — secret (hr salary data) entrusted in professional capacity, disclosure to unauthorized party (personal gmail), no legal requirement for disclosure. elements missing — employment contract/nda explicitly classifying data as 'secret entrusted in professional capacity', confirmation disclosure was not legally mandated, evidence of professional-capacity relationship. prosecution strength: strong.

uae federal decree-law 34/2021 art. 9 (data destruction/alteration): elements met — (1) unauthorized access confirmed via privilege violation (t1078, t1548); (2) data manipulation confirmed: steganographic copying (t1041), external disclosure (t1566.001), destruction of source and logs (t1070.004, t1070.001); (3) information system confirmed (corporate hr system, /hr/restricted/ path); (4) intent/premeditation evidenced by pre-installed openstego, scripted sequence, out-of-hours access, dlp bypass. elements missing — formal hr/it written confirmation of non-authorization; forensic hash verification of steganographic payload; dlp/mail-gateway logs with carrier-file hash; system audit logs for exact command sequence; confirmation deleted file was the specific salary file. prosecution strength: strong.

uae federal decree-law 34/2021 art. 11 (ransomware/extortion): not applicable — no threat, blackmail, encryption-for-ransom, or compulsion behaviour identified. should be excluded from charge sheet to avoid diluting art. 9 prosecution. prosecution strength: weak (excluded).

federal decree-law 34/2021 art. 2 (unlawful access): elements met — unauthorised access to information system, without permission of owner, targeting a specific restricted file. elements missing — formal system-owner attestation of no access grant; correlation of domain-account session to exact exfiltration timestamp; confirmation whether rdp (t1021.004) was the access vector. prosecution strength: strong.

federal decree-law 34/2021 art. 9 (data destruction / alteration / unauthorised copying): elements met — unauthorised copying (stego embedding), disclosure (email exfiltration), destruction (file and log deletion) of data on an information system. elements missing — forensic stego-payload extraction and hash verification against staff_salaries_2009.xlsx; recovery of deleted files; gmail-side delivery confirmation; proof deletion was by ann and not automated policy. prosecution strength: moderate.

uae penal code art. 379 (breach of confidentiality / trade secrets): elements met — secret entrusted in professional capacity (hr salary data); disclosure to unauthorised third party (personal gmail). elements missing — formal nda/role confirmation covering hr salary data; evidence data was not already public; quantification of harm (number of employees exposed). prosecution strength: moderate.

federal decree-law 34/2021 art. 9 (uae) – unauthorized disclosure/copying of data: element 1 (unauthorized access) met — ann lacked hr_admin membership; element 2 (data manipulation/disclosure) met — copy, stego-embed, and email to unauthorized recipient; element 3 (information system) met — corporate workstation, email, and hr system qualify. missing: byte-for-byte stego payload verification, confirmed third-party recipient identity, explicit failed-authorization log, and resolution of retroactivity (2009 incident vs. 2021 enactment). prosecution strength: strong.
federal decree-law 34/2021 art. 11 (uae) – ransomware/extortion via it: not met — no coercion, ransom demand, or compulsion evidenced. prosecution strength: weak. not applicable on current record.

federal decree-law 34/2021 art.9 (data destruction/alteration): elements met — data manipulation via stego embedding, unauthorised copying/disclosure to external account, destruction of data (source files + shell history). elements missing — explicit written confirmation of lack of authorisation (insider access blurs threshold), state-secret classification for aggravated sentencing, temporal applicability (incident 2009; operative law was federal law no. 12/2006). prosecution strength: moderate.

uae penal code art.379 (breach of confidentiality / trade secrets): elements met — disclosure of confidential hr data entrusted in professional capacity, no legal compulsion or employer authorisation, concealment via steganography indicating intent to hide. elements missing — definitive confirmation of gmail account ownership, proof of third-party receipt/use, signed nda or policy explicitly designating staff salaries as protected secret. prosecution strength: strong.

federal decree-law 34/2021 art. 2 (unlawful access): elements met — unauthorized access to information system, without permission of owner, ann lacked hr_admin group membership, access outside permitted hours. elements missing — formal system-ownership confirmation, independent server-side audit log corroboration, jurisdictional situs confirmation. prosecution strength: strong

federal decree-law 34/2021 art. 9 (data destruction/alteration): elements met — deletion of .bash_history, deletion of source files, steganographic alteration of annualreport.jpg, unauthorized copying to external account. elements missing — forensic attribution of deletion to ann specifically (vs. system process), legal characterization of steganographic embedding as 'alteration' vs. 'creation', confirmation data qualifies as being 'on a computer network or information system'. prosecution strength: strong

uae penal code art. 379 (breach of confidentiality/trade secrets): elements met — disclosure of restricted data to external personal account, no legal authorization, professional-capacity context suggested. elements missing — employment contract and job description confirming 'entrusted in professional capacity', legal characterization of salary data as a 'secret' under art. 379, confirmation whether self-retention constitutes 'disclosure'. prosecution strength: moderate

federal decree-law 34/2021 art. 11 (ransomware/extortion): not applicable — no threat, blackmail, encryption-for-ransom, or compulsion evidenced. excluded from recommended charges. prosecution strength: weak (excluded)

uae penal code art. 379 (breach of confidentiality / trade secrets): elements met — disclosure of secret (salary data), professional entrustment (insider hr access), lack of authorisation (personal gmail destination), intent to conceal (steganography + deletion). elements missing — formal nda/contractual obligation documentation, 2009-era policy classification of the file as a 'secret', affirmative exclusion of legal-mandate exception. prosecution strength: strong.

federal decree-law 34/2021 art. 9 (data destruction / unauthorised copying): elements met — unauthorised copying into stego carrier, external disclosure, deliberate destruction of shell history and source files, data on an information system. elements missing — rbac matrix confirming no policy exception, byte-level payload confirmation, aggravated-tier data classification, independent forensic verification of deletion. critical caveat: conduct occurred in 2009; fdl 34/2021 was enacted in 2021 and does not apply retroactively. prosecution strength: moderate (subject to temporal applicability).

federal decree-law 34/2021 art. 2 (unlawful access): elements met — access to an information system. elements missing — ann likely held valid credentials; the issue is misuse of authorised access, not unauthorised entry. better characterised under art. 9 or penal code art. 379. same temporal caveat applies. prosecution strength: weak.

federal decree-law 34/2021 art.9 (data destruction/alteration, uae): elements met — unauthorized access (t1078/t1548.003), data copying via steganographic embedding (t1560.001), disclosure via email to external account (t1041/t1567.002), destruction of source and history (t1070.004/t1070.001), corporate information system as the affected system. elements missing — no evidence of third-party recipient beyond ann's own account, no publication to broader audience, no state-secrets aggravating tier, and critical temporal issue: incident date 2009-11-16 predates the 2021 decree; governing law at time of offence (pre-2012 uae penal code / federal law 5/2012) must be confirmed. prosecution strength: moderate.

federal decree-law 34/2021 art.11 (ransomware/extortion, uae): not applicable. no threat, blackmail, encryption-for-ransom, or compensation demand identified in any artefact. prosecution strength: weak (no evidentiary basis).

uae penal code art.379 (breach of confidentiality / trade secrets): elements met — confidential data disclosed externally, professional capacity, unauthorised disclosure. elements missing — formal nda, explicit policy designation of the file as a protected secret, confirmation that gmail account is not ann's own. prosecution strength: strong.

federal decree-law 34/2021 art.9 (data destruction / alteration / unauthorised copying): elements met — steganographic copying/alteration, deliberate deletion of shell history and source file, premeditation via pre-installed tool. elements missing — forensic recovery of deleted artefacts, openstego installation timestamp/source, explicit 'without authorization' determination for the copying act. prosecution strength: moderate.

federal decree-law 34/2021 art.2 (unlawful access): elements met — access to restricted information system, privilege violation, use of valid credentials. elements missing — formal rbac/access-control matrix, explicit denial from system owner, granular access logs for the 02:28–02:53 window. prosecution strength: moderate.

uae penal code art. 379 (breach of confidentiality / trade secrets): core elements met — secret entrusted in professional capacity, deliberate disclosure to unauthorised third party, concealment via steganography. missing: formal nda/confidentiality clause, explicit classification policy, identity of ultimate beneficiary. prosecution strength: strong. temporal applicability: 2009 conduct falls under pre-2021 uae penal code provisions; art. 379 is the correct historical charge.

federal decree-law 34/2021 art. 9 (data destruction / alteration): elements partially met — deliberate deletion of shell history and source files, alteration of annualreport.jpg. missing: formal authorisation matrix, legal characterisation of steganographic embedding as 'alteration', quantification of harm. critical temporal defect: fdl 34/2021 enacted in 2021; conduct occurred in 2009. retroactive application is constitutionally barred under uae law. prosecution strength: moderate (contingent on re-characterisation).

federal decree-law 34/2021 art. 2 (unlawful access): core element 'without permission of owner' is contradicted by the insider-threat profile — ann held a legitimate account and likely had some level of system access. missing: proof that specific file/system was outside granted permissions. same temporal defect as art. 9. prosecution strength: weak.

federal decree-law 34/2021 art. 11 (ransomware / extortion): not applicable — no threat, blackmail, encryption-for-ransom, or coercive communication is evidenced in any behaviour. excluded from recommended charges.

uae penal code art. 379 (breach of confidentiality / trade secrets): elements met — secret entrusted in professional capacity (hr salary data), disclosure to personal gmail outside corporate environment, absence of legal authorisation, deliberate and premeditated conduct. elements missing — precise exfiltrated payload content not independently confirmed, identity linkage between 'ann' and gmail account holder not formally established, no formal nda produced. prosecution strength: strong.

federal decree-law 34/2021 art. 9 (data destruction / alteration / unauthorised copying): elements met — unauthorised access beyond group scope, data copied and stego-embedded, deletion of shell history and source files constituting unauthorised alteration. elements missing — quantification of data set copied, clarification whether deletion occurred on corporate system vs. local workstation, statutory definition of 'information system' requires technical attestation. prosecution strength: moderate.

federal decree-law 34/2021 art. 2 (unlawful access to information system): elements met — access beyond granted permissions, corporate file-server and email infrastructure as information system, circumvention of access controls via dlp bypass. elements missing — formal rbac/access-control matrix proving explicit restriction, demonstration that scope limitation was communicated and enforceable, technical attestation that system qualifies under art. 2 definition. prosecution strength: moderate.

federal decree-law 34/2021 art.2 (unlawful access to information system): elements met — ssh access to organizational system; off-hours timing. elements missing — ann held valid credentials (insider), undermining 'without permission' element; no evidence the specific directory was outside her authorized scope (rbac logs absent); no credential theft or authentication bypass; temporal applicability gap. prosecution strength: weak

federal decree-law 34/2021 art.11 (ransomware/extortion): no elements met. no extortion demand, no encryption for coercion, no payment demand. not applicable — exclude from charge framework. prosecution strength: weak (inapplicable)

federal decree-law 34/2021 art.2 (unlawful access): elements met — unauthorised access to information system, without permission of owner, via privilege escalation or credential misuse. elements missing — formal written denial of access by it department, confirmation that no temporary/emergency access grant was issued. prosecution strength: strong

federal decree-law 34/2021 art.2 (unlawful access): elements met — access to an information system, access to a restricted dataset. elements missing — ann held valid credentials (t1078.004), so the 'without permission' element is vulnerable; differentiation between authorised system access and unauthorised data-subset access is not established; classification of the hr system under art.2 definitions is unconfirmed. prosecution strength: weak

federal decree-law 34/2021 art. 2 (unlawful access to information systems): elements met — access to information system, data designated restricted. elements missing — proof ann lacked legitimate read access, access-control denial logs, privilege-escalation evidence. if ann had role-based read access, this charge fails. prosecution strength: weak.

uae penal code art. 379 (breach of confidentiality / trade secrets): elements met — secret entrusted in professional capacity, disclosure to external party, no legal obligation to disclose, confidential nature of data. elements missing — explicit written non-authorisation from data owner, confirmed recipient identity, contemporaneous corporate policy classifying the file as restricted. prosecution strength: strong.

federal decree-law 34/2021 art. 2 (unlawful access): elements met — information system involved, data accessed and retrieved. elements missing — proof access was 'without permission' (insider may have had read access), temporal applicability (2009 offence vs 2021 law; non-retroactivity likely bars application), documentation of authorised access scope. prosecution strength: weak.

federal decree-law 34/2021 art. 9 (unauthorised data destruction/alteration/copying): elements met — destruction, alteration, and copying all evidenced; deliberate anti-forensic intent. elements missing — temporal applicability (same non-retroactivity barrier), proof deletion was 'without authorization', forensic confirmation of recoverability of deleted artefacts. prosecution strength: moderate.

federal decree-law 34/2021 art. 2 (unlawful access): elements met — access to corporate information systems. elements missing — the critical 'without permission' element is not clearly established given ann's hr-adjacent role; no credential theft, privilege escalation, or access-control bypass evidenced; better characterised as unauthorised use (art. 9) or breach of confidence (art. 379). prosecution strength: weak.
